text:
Amelia: Quick flag — celeste20b int4 canary is showing two pain points: OOMs on long windows (>=4096) and a measurable ROUGE regression on summarization. Dropping raw notes here.

Rishi: Logs or a minimal repro?

Amelia: Pasting top-of-stack and alloc trace we saw (reduced):
```
[2026-06-14T11:05:12Z] gpu0: alloc 128MB failed -> trying compaction -> small free blocks -> OOM
Trace: runtime.cpp:452 allocateKVCache -> mempool.cpp:123 alloc_chunk -> oom
free slots: 4, largest_free: 24MB, total_free: 160MB, reserved: 256MB
```

Jack: That pattern smells like fragmentation (lots of small frees, largest_free << total_free). Prefetch + large max_new_tokens will amplify this.

Maya: What are the canary batching/defaults right now?

Amelia: Canary config: `max_new_tokens: 512`, `batch_timeout_ms: 12`, `max_batch_tokens: 16384`, `prefetch: enabled`, `reserve_slots: 1.0`

Jack: Two immediate experiments: 1) lower `max_new_tokens` default to 256 for this variant, 2) reduce `batch_timeout_ms` to 8 and `max_batch_tokens` to 8192. Also try turning off prefetch initially. Small batches + smaller max_new reduces long-lived allocations so fewer fragmentation hits.

Rishi: On the quality side we ran the summarization eval: int4 vs fp16 baseline => ROUGE-L -1.2, SacreBLEU -0.8, avg ppl +2.3 on the eval set. So there's a quantization quality delta we need to address.

Maya: Could be LayerNorm / softmax scaling noise. Any per-layer calibration applied?

Amelia: We used per-tensor static calibration from ptq script. No mixed-cast tweaks.

Jack: Quick mitigation: enable `cast_layernorm_fp16: true` and `softmax_cast_fp16: true` for the int4 runtime path. That often recovers the few-pt drops without full fp16 memory cost. Also enable `kv_cache_shrink_threshold: 0.6` so the runtime tries to compact when live utilization drops.

Rishi: Good. Also add an eval gate in the canary: require ROUGE-L delta >= -0.5 vs fp16, else fallback.

deploy-bot: deploy 2259876500: canary celeste20b-int4 v1.3 -> 5% traffic.

Amelia: Rolling the patch: set `max_new_tokens: 256`, `batch_timeout_ms: 8`, `max_batch_tokens: 8192`, `prefetch: false`, `cast_layernorm_fp16: true`, `kv_cache_shrink_threshold: 0.6`, `reserve_slots: 1.5` and gating eval in canary.

Jack: When you flip `reserve_slots` to 1.5, it increases memory headroom for large windows which helps avoid fragment-triggered OOMs at the cost of lower density. It's a good safety canary.

Amelia: Starting new canary run now with the patch. Hitting same long prompts (~3k tokens) repeatedly. Will call out if any OOM.

infra-bot: metric created: `celeste20b.int4.slot_frag_ratio` (rolling 5m), alert threshold 0.3.

Maya: Also add a synthetic long-window test in our CI eval — a few thousand-step generation to surface fragmentation regressions before rollout.

Rishi: For the quality regression: if `cast_layernorm_fp16` doesn't recover to within -0.5 ROUGE-L, plan B is to keep int4 but set routing rule: `if prompt_length > 2048 -> route to fp16_celeste20b` (fallback), and update SDK model profile.

Amelia: Update: after ~45 minutes into canary (5%): no OOMs so far on repeated 3k prompts. `slot_frag_ratio` dropped from 0.42 -> 0.21.

Jack: Nice. Any eval numbers yet?

Amelia: Preliminary canary eval (small sample): ROUGE-L delta now -0.4, ppl delta +0.9. Within gate.

Maya: Great. Next steps: 1) bump canary to 20% for 4h while keeping gating, 2) if stable, set model default `max_new_tokens` to 256 in model catalog and publish a note in SDK: "celeste20b-int4: recommended defaults for production: max_new_tokens=256, batch_timeout_ms=8, no prefetch for >2048 windows".

Rishi: Also capture a short internal note about which workloads should prefer fp16 (long summarization, multi-turn doc writing). Add a quality regression alert to Optimize so users see it.

deploy-bot: deploy 2259876575: canary celeste20b-int4 v1.4 -> 20% traffic.

Amelia: Rolling to 20% now. Will run a longer eval job overnight. If anyone wants to block, speak now. :eyes:

Jack: One sticky item to follow up: we should instrument per-kernel alloc sizes in the runtime so we can better distinguish fragmentation caused by many small allocs vs a few mid-sized ones. Filed infra ticket.

Maya: I'll add the long-window CI case. Also will add a quick how-to in devex for migrators about the `cast_layernorm_fp16` knob.

Rishi: If after full rollout we still see corner-case OOMs, consider a permanent routing policy: prefer int4 for short/medium windows, fallback to fp16 for >4096.

Amelia: Thanks team. I'll post the final canary summary and the recommended model-profile PR once overnight eval finishes. :party-parrot:

Jack: thanks — nice incremental approach, +1 to not rushing defaults.

Amelia: (closing) will add a quick changelog note in the model onboarding doc and update the dedicated config template.
